correctness.rationale: From the actual ellipse Chebyshev planar orthogonality, reconstructed K_2m(z,0)=sum_{k=0}^m (-1)^k(2k+1)U_2k(z/c)/U_2k(t), with identical odd-degree center slice. Thin-ellipse limit is (−1)^m U_m(2(z/a)²−1), giving exactly 2m simple interior real roots for sufficiently small b/a. Near-disk rescaling yields P_m(v)=sum_{k=0}^m (−1)^k(2k+1)v^k; its negative-real exclusion and Newton inequality contradiction for m≥2 show ≥4 nonreal roots. Independently recomputed K4 rational quadratic in x=(z/a)² and Δ=64(u−1)²u⁴Q(u+1/u), with Q(y)=225y⁴−600y³−14600y²−44000y−32624. Unique root y>2 gives strict four-real/two-double/four-nonreal transition; degree2 threshold x<1 iff u<1/3. Symbolic identities checked independently, not only a packaged VERIFY_OK.

value.rationale: The root locus of the finite complex polynomial reproducing kernel on an ellipse is a natural analytic question, unlike generic infinite Bergman zeros. It yields a sharp first degree and exact shape transition with a nontrivial Newton obstruction for arbitrary degree; the explicit algebraic cutoff is reusable in finite-rank planar kernel studies.

limitations: The center slice is a finite-rank polynomial K_d(z,0), not the infinite Bergman kernel; near-circle nonreal zeros may leave ellipse.
No global all-m transition uniqueness, no off-center classification, no independent formal proof.
